result.summary: The page is mostly well-formed, but the 'Fastest near you' carousel shows noticeable layout misalignment: the middle card (Smash Bros Burgers) is vertically offset from its neighbors, and card images have inconsistent sizes/aspect ratios. There is also a hard text cutoff ('Trattoria Piccol') without ellipsis, and a category chip is clipped at the screen edge.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' carousel, the middle card (Smash Bros Burgers) is vertically misaligned — its image starts lower and its title/price sit lower than the adjacent cards (Green Bowl Poké and Trattoria), making the row look broken.
issues.suggestion: Align all carousel cards to a common top edge and use a fixed, uniform image height so titles and delivery prices sit on the same baseline.

issues.description: Card thumbnails in 'Fastest near you' have inconsistent heights/aspect ratios (the poké image is taller than the burger image), contributing to the uneven row.
issues.suggestion: Enforce a consistent aspect ratio (e.g., 4:3 or 16:9) with object-fit cover for all carousel thumbnails.

issues.description: The third card title is hard-clipped as 'Trattoria Piccol' with no ellipsis, which looks like broken text rather than intentional carousel overflow.
issues.suggestion: Apply text truncation with an ellipsis (…) or ensure the text is clipped along with the card container so partial words aren't shown against the page background.

issues.description: A category filter chip after 'Healthy' is cut off at the right screen edge with only a sliver visible, giving little affordance of what it is.
issues.suggestion: Adjust the chip carousel so the peeking item shows enough of its label (e.g., 30–40% visible) to signal horizontal scrollability, or add a fade/gradient edge.

issues.description: The bottom pizza card in 'Popular right now' is abruptly cut off by the tab bar with no visual separation, so its content collides with the navigation area.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding/safe-area inset to the scroll container or a subtle shadow/divider on the tab bar so content doesn't appear clipped underneath it.
